newsitem.title: USA: New Orleans Industrial Canal partially reopened.
newsitem.headline: New Orleans Industrial Canal partially reopened.

text.p: The Industrial Canal reopened Tuesday to one-way traffic only as authorities continued to off-load several damaged containers leaking toxic chemicals, the Coast Guard Marine Safety Office reported.
The canal, connecting the Mississippi River to the Mississippi River Gulf Outlet and Lake Pontchartrain, is considered a major industrial link for barge traffic.
The Coast Guard said Tuesday that more than two dozen barges and tugs that had been backed up have moved through the canal.

The canal was closed Saturday after the barge Ponce Trader, owned by Pacific Marine Leasing of Portland, Ore., arrived from Houston with damaged containers, some of which were leaking chemicals, including vinyl acetate and toluene di-isocyanate, the Coast Guard said.

One container collapsed late Friday, dumping 27 containers into the Gulf of Mexico during rough weather, according to the Coast Guard Marine Safety Office at Morgan City, La. By Monday, six of the lost containers were under tow and the location of the others unknown.
None of the lost containers was believed to be carrying hazardous materials, and one contained a car. The specific destinations of the containers were not known.

A spokeswoman for SeaLand, where the barge with damaged containers is being off-loaded, said Tuesday that the firm normally is closed on weekends and the only backlog resulted from the Veterans' Day holiday closing Monday.
